body.zh-Hant: 1863年生於馬德里，在博洛尼亞完成部分法學學業並取得法學博士。他於1884年加入自由黨，兩年後開始當議員，1893年獲封羅馬諾內斯伯爵。
body.en: Born in Madrid in 1863, he studied law, partly at Bologna, where he took his doctorate. He joined the Liberal Party in 1884, began his career as a deputy two years later, and in 1893 became Count of Romanones.

citations.quote: Nacido el Sat Aug 08 00:00:00 CET 1863 en Madrid.
Hizo la carrera de Leyes, parte de ella en Bolonia, donde se doctoró en Derecho.
Su vida política estuvo vinculada al partido liberal al cual se afilió en 1884
dos años más tarde comenzó su trayectoria como diputado
citations.evidenceNote: 「兩年後」相對於1884年入黨，即1886年；同頁另寫「Diputado por Guadalajara entre 1886 y 1936」

citations.quote: 1893 Graf von Romanones

heading.en: Mayor of Madrid and early ministries

body.zh-Hant: 他在1894至1895年及1897至1899年擔任馬德里市長；1901至1902年任公共教育與美術部長，1905至1906年與1906至1907年任內政部長，1910年再任公共教育與美術部長。
body.en: He served as mayor of Madrid in 1894-1895 and 1897-1899, as minister of public instruction and fine arts in 1901-1902, as interior minister in 1905-1906 and 1906-1907, and again as minister of public instruction and fine arts in 1910.

citations.quote: 1894-1895 und 1897-1899 Bürgermeister von Madrid
1901-1902 Minister für öffentlichen Unterricht und schöne Künste
1905-1906 Innenminister
1906-1907 Innenminister

heading.en: President of the Congress and three premierships

body.zh-Hant: 1910年6月16日起他三度擔任眾議院議長，最後一段至1912年11月18日。他首度出任首相始於1912年11月14日，其後又於1915年12月9日至1917年4月19日、1918年12月5日至1919年4月15日主持內閣。
body.en: He presided over the Congress of Deputies three times from 16 June 1910, the last period ending on 18 November 1912. He first presided over the Council of Ministers from 14 November 1912, and presided over it again from 9 December 1915 to 19 April 1917 and from 5 December 1918 to 15 April 1919.

citations.quote: Presidió el Congreso de los Diputados en tres ocasiones
la primera entre el 14 de noviembre y el 31 de diciembre de 1912
la tercera entre el 9 de diciembre de 1915 y el 19 de abril de 1917
la cuarta y última, entre el 5 de diciembre de 1918 y el 15 de abril de 1919
1912-1913, 1915-1917 und 1918-1919 Ministerpräsident

heading.zh-Hant: 部長、獨裁中斷與共和國
heading.en: Further ministries, the dictatorship and the Republic

body.zh-Hant: 1918年他擔任過司法部長、公共教育與美術部長及外交部長，1922至1923年再任司法部長。1923年9月至1930年1月普里莫·德里維拉獨裁期間，他的政治生涯中斷。1931年任外交部長；同年4月14日，他須與共和國臨時政府商定無暴力的過渡，以保障國王及其家人的性命。
body.en: In 1918 he held the ministries of justice, public instruction and foreign affairs, and in 1922-1923 he was again minister of justice. His political life was interrupted between September 1923 and January 1930 during the dictatorship of Miguel Primo de Rivera. In 1931 he was foreign minister, and on 14 April he had to agree a non-violent transition with the provisional government of the Republic to guarantee the life of the King and his family.

body.zh-Hant: 1943年3月16日至1946年4月24日，他以文化機構代表身分擔任第一屆議會的議員（procurador）。他曾任聖費爾南多皇家美術學院院長與馬德里文學藝術俱樂部（Ateneo）主席，1950年在馬德里去世。
body.en: From 16 March 1943 to 24 April 1946 he sat as a procurador for the cultural institutions in the first legislature. He was director of the Royal Academy of Fine Arts of San Fernando and president of the Ateneo de Madrid, and died in Madrid in 1950.

body.zh-Hant: 曼努埃爾二世1889年生於里斯本，是國王卡洛斯一世與王后瑪麗亞·阿梅莉亞的次子。1908年2月，父王與王儲路易斯親王同遭暗殺，他因此被推上王位。
body.en: Manuel II was born in Lisbon in 1889, the second son of King Carlos I and Queen Maria Amélia. In February 1908 his father and the crown prince, Infante Luís Filipe, were killed together in a double regicide, which brought him to the throne.

citations.quote: Nato a Lisbona il 19 marzo 1889
citations.evidenceNote: 原文日期；僅取年份入正文

citations.quote: Figlio secondogenito del re Carlo I e della regina Maria Amelia
fu chiamato al trono dal doppio regicidio
dal doppio regicidio ( i febbraio 1908)
citations.evidenceNote: 原文「i febbraio」疑為「1 febbraio」之掃描誤植；僅取年月

citations.quote: il re Carlo e il principe ereditario infante D. Luis

body.zh-Hant: 他登基時尚未滿二十歲，處境極為艱難。不得人心的大臣若昂·弗朗科遭撤換，改由海軍上將費雷拉·杜·阿馬拉爾接任，後者恢復了葡萄牙的議會制。
body.en: He reached the crown unexpectedly, not yet twenty years old, at a very difficult moment. The disliked minister João Franco was removed and replaced by Admiral F. J. Ferreira do Amaral, who restored the parliamentary system in Portugal.

citations.quote: non ancora ventenne
in momenti difficilissimi
la rimozione dell'inviso ministro Joăo Franco
ammiraglio F. J. Ferreira do Amaral
che ristabilì in Portogallo il sistema parlamentare
letzter König von Portugal, regierte 1908-1910

body.zh-Hant: 儘管年輕國王頗得人緣，也努力為王朝贏回民心，共和黨仍加倍活動，尤其攻擊被指偏袒保守派的太后。1910年10月4日革命爆發，他被迫出逃，原想前往波爾圖，因恐被叛變軍艦俘獲而改往直布羅陀。
body.en: Despite the young king's personal popularity and his efforts to win back favour for the dynasty, the Republican Party redoubled its activity, attacking above all the queen mother, whom it accused of favouring conservative elements. When the revolution broke out on 4 October 1910 he had to flee; he first meant to go to Oporto, but the danger of capture by rebel ships led him to head for Gibraltar.

citations.quote: il partito repubblicano raddoppiò di attività per rovesciarla
rivolgendo soprattutto i suoi attacchi alla regina madre
Scoppiato il moto rivoluzionario del 4 ottobre 1910, dovette fuggire.
Voleva dapprima recarsi a Oporto
lo indusse a dirigersi su Gibilterra
Malgrado le simpatie personali che ispirava il giovane re
i suoi sforzi per riacquistare alla dinastia il favore popolare
che accusava di favorire gli elementi conservatori
il pericolo di esser catturato dalle navi ribelli

body.zh-Hant: 他隨後與太后及波爾圖公爵登上英王喬治五世派來的皇家遊艇前往英國，此後在特威克納姆過著私人生活。1913年他與霍亨索倫—西格馬林根的奧古斯塔·維多利亞公主結婚，1932年7月2日在特威克納姆去世。
body.en: Some days later he embarked with the queen mother and the Duke of Oporto on the British royal yacht sent by King George V, and from then on lived privately at Twickenham. In 1913 he married Princess Augusta Victoria of Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen, and he died at Twickenham on 2 July 1932.

citations.quote: sopra lo yacht reale inglese inviatogli da re Giorgio V
si ritrasse d'indi in poi a vita privata a Twickenham
Nel 1913 sposò la principessa Augusta Vittoria di Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen
morto a Twickenham (Inghilterra) il 2 luglio 1932
con la regina madre e il duca di Oporto s'imbarcò per l'Inghilterra

body.zh-Hant: 饒爾達尼亞出身於喬治亞西部的小貴族家庭，早年在第比利斯東正教神學院受教育，後前往華沙深造，在那裡接觸到馬克思主義。1890年代初，他在喬治亞進步刊物《Kvali》上發表文章，啟發了後來被稱為「第三代」（mesame dasi）的年輕激進分子。
body.en: Noe Zhordania came from a petty noble family in western Georgia. He was educated at the Tiflis Orthodox Seminary and then went to Warsaw for further education, where he was introduced to Marxism. His writings in the Georgian progressive journal Kvali in the early 1890s inspired the young radicals soon known as the mesame dasi (third generation).

heading.zh-Hant: 孟什維克領袖與杜馬議員

body.zh-Hant: 到1905年，他已加入俄國社會民主黨較溫和的孟什維克派，並帶領絕大多數喬治亞社會民主黨人同行。1906年他當選第一屆國家杜馬議員，數月後沙皇解散杜馬，他與其他激進派簽署《維堡宣言》抗議，被迫轉入地下。
body.en: By 1905 he had affiliated with the more moderate wing of Russian Social Democracy, the Mensheviks, and took the bulk of Georgian Social Democrats along with him. In 1906 he was elected to the first State Duma; within a few months the tsar dissolved it, and Zhordania and other radicals signed the Vyborg Manifesto in protest, after which he was forced into the political underground.

heading.zh-Hant: 革命與喬治亞民主共和國
heading.en: Revolution and the Democratic Republic of Georgia

body.zh-Hant: 1917年革命爆發後，他出任第比利斯蘇維埃主席，反對同年十月布爾什維克在彼得格勒的勝利，並在1918年5月26日宣布喬治亞獨立的過程中發揮關鍵作用。他當選共和國總統（德國權威檔記為總理，1918至1921年），任職至1921年2月紅軍入侵。
body.en: After the outbreak of revolution in 1917 he became chairman of the Tiflis Soviet, opposed the Bolshevik victory in Petrograd in October of that year, and was instrumental in the declaration of Georgian independence on 26 May 1918. He was elected president of the republic (recorded as prime minister, 1918-1921, in the German authority file) and served until the Red Army invasion of February 1921.

body.zh-Hant: 流亡法國期間，他策劃對共產黨政府的起義，但1924年8月的叛亂遭蘇聯血腥鎮壓。他晚年主要在法國度過，撰寫回憶錄，並與西方情報機構合作對抗蘇聯，仍被公認為一個內部紛爭不斷的運動的領袖。
body.en: From exile in France he planned an insurrection against the Communist government, but the revolt of August 1924 was bloodily suppressed by the Soviets. He spent his last years in exile, largely in France, writing his memoirs and conspiring with Western intelligence agencies against the Soviets, still the acknowledged leader of a movement whose members fought bitterly with one another.
